Elonites
EE-lon-ites
n. (proper name; a family of the tribe of Zebulun)
Hebrew 'Eloni, the family-name formed from Elon, a son of Zebulun. The personal name is connected with 'elon, an oak or a terebinth.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Elonites are named once: “Of the sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Sardites: of Elon, the family of the Elonites: of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites” (Numbers 26:26). Zebulun was Leah's sixth son and Jacob's tenth, and the tribe drew a portion in the north, in the hill country and down toward the lake. Scripture says little of Zebulun in the histories, and then says something very great about the tribe's territory. Isaiah names the land of Zebulun as the first place the light would come: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali … in Galilee of the nations” (Isaiah 9:1), and Matthew quotes it of Christ's ministry at Capernaum (Matthew 4:13-16). Nazareth stood in Zebulun's allotment. The Elonites are a family in the tribe whose hills the Lord walked and whose villages first heard Him preach. The census that enrolled them for a portion of ground was enrolling them, as it turned out, for the ground on which the gospel would be first proclaimed.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Elonites is a Hebrew family-name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Elonites is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears once, in Numbers 26:26.

The family descends from Elon, a son of Zebulun.

The personal name is connected with 'elon, an oak or terebinth.

The Sardites and Jahleelites are named with them in the same verse.

Key Scripture

Num 26:26 — "Of the sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Sardites: of Elon, the family of the Elonites: of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites."

Gen 46:14 — "And the sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel."

Isa 9:1 — "Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations."

Mat 4:13 — "And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:"

Modern Corruption

Galilee is treated as a backwater of no account; prophecy had marked it as the first ground the light would touch.

expand to see more

Zebulun's northern allotment is routinely written off as marginal, and the Galilee of the Gospels with it — a provincial district far from where anything mattered. Isaiah had said otherwise seven centuries before, and Matthew cites him to show that Christ's choice of Capernaum was no accident of convenience but the fulfilling of a word.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God appoints the ground as well as the hour. The land divided to Zebulun's families by lot in the plains of Moab was the land on which the Light of the world would open His mouth. A portion assigned by a cast lot in the fortieth year was being assigned by the God who had already written Isaiah 9.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Eloni, from 'elon, an oak; the family of Elon son of Zebulun, enrolled in Numbers 26.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Eloni, a family-name formed from the personal name Elon.

The name is connected with 'elon, an oak or terebinth.

Elon is the second-named son of Zebulun in Genesis 46:14.

An Elon of Zebulun also judged Israel ten years, Judges 12:11-12.

Numbers 26:27 totals Zebulun at threescore thousand and five hundred.
